Cost Guide · 2026 Pricing

What Tree Work Actually Costs in NE Ohio — Aaron's Confirmed 2026 Pricing

Six services, four pricing tiers per service, five factors that shift the number. Everything Aaron talks through on the free property walk — plus the questions to ask any tree service you're comparing.

10 min read Updated Aug 2026 Free · No signup

AR

{{global.owner_name}}

Owner · Operations Lead · 17 years of NE Ohio tree work

Published Aug 12, 2026 Updated Aug 12, 2026 10 min read
Share

Every price in this guide comes from {{global.owner_name}}'s own 2026 job records — no aspirational ranges, no bait-and-switch estimates, no "call for pricing" fog. If it's on this page, it's what Roubic actually charges.

How Roubic Prices — The 5 Factors

Every Roubic estimate comes from the same 5 variables. When Aaron walks a property, he's answering these five questions before writing the number:

  1. Tree size — height + trunk diameter determine crew, rigging, and time.
  2. Site access — driveway width, gate clearance, overhead lines, and lawn-load rating.
  3. Adjacent structures — proximity to house, garage, fence, or septic determines whether we can fell or need sectional rigging.
  4. Disposal — full chip haul-off (standard) vs. leave logs on site (some clients want firewood).
  5. Village permit — Pepper Pike (24" DBH), Moreland Hills, Gates Mills (18") — Roubic files these in-house.

Those five factors explain 95% of the range. The other 5% is weather, urgency (emergency vs scheduled), and crane requirements for very-large jobs.

Tree Removal — $400 to $5,000+

Removal is the highest-volume service Roubic offers. Four pricing tiers based on tree size, with pricing tightening for restricted access on any tier.

Small (< 30 ft)Fell + chip haul
$400–$800
Medium (30–60 ft)Sectional lower + chip
$650–$950
Large (60–80 ft)Climbing rig + full haul
$850–$2,000
Very Large / Crane80+ ft or restricted access
$2,000–$5,000+

Emergency removal (24/7 line, storm response, tree-on-structure) typically adds 20–30% for after-hours callout, but includes the insurance-documentation packet at no extra cost.

Tree Trimming & Pruning — $375 to $800+

ANSI A300 pruning applies on every Roubic trimming job. Pricing tracks with tree size and access, same as removal, but the labor curve is flatter because we're preserving the tree rather than dismantling it.

Ornamental (< 20 ft)Shaping, deadwood, small crown
$375–$500
Mid-Size Deciduous (20–40 ft)Crown thinning, structural pruning
$500–$800
Large Canopy (40+ ft)Climbing rig, sectional pruning
Priced on-site

Species-specific care (oak wilt windows, ash-borer preservation attempts) is included in the base price when Aaron walks the property.

Stump Grinding — $275 Minimum

Simple pricing formula: $275 minimum charge plus $8 per inch of stump diameter, ground to 6–12" below grade. Full excavation removal (for re-planting or hardscape) is priced separately.

Small Stump (< 12" diameter)$275 min applies
$275
Medium (12–24" diameter)$275 + $8/inch after 12"
$275–$375
Large (24–36" diameter)$275 + $8/inch
$375–$465
Multi-Stump Discount3+ stumps same visit
10% off

Land Clearing — $1,500 to $20,000+ per Acre

Land clearing pricing depends on density — a few scattered trees over an acre is vastly different from clearing dense underbrush on a wooded lot.

Light DensityScattered trees, moderate brush
$1,500–$3,000/acre
Medium DensityMixed trees + underbrush
$3,000–$8,000/acre
Heavy DensityWooded lot, thick undergrowth
$5,000–$20,000+/acre

Driveway or build-site prep is often a fixed-scope job rather than acreage-based — Aaron confirms scope on the property walk.

Storm Damage & Emergency — $500 to $8,000+

Storm work is priced by scope and access rather than tree size — a small tree on a garage roof can cost more than a large tree in an open yard.

Fallen Tree — Open AccessNo structure impact, standard removal
$500–$1,500
Tree on StructureRoof, garage, fence
$1,500–$4,000
Multi-Tree Storm CleanupWhole-property clearing
$3,000–$8,000+

Every storm job includes a full insurance-documentation packet — photos, written scope, signed estimate — ready for direct submission to your homeowner's carrier.

Firewood Delivery — $180 to $450 per Cord

Seasoned hardwood only. Roubic never delivers green (unseasoned) firewood. Pricing tracks with delivery distance and stacking service.

Face Cord Delivered1/3 of a full cord
$180–$220
Full Cord Delivered4×4×8 ft, seasoned
$350–$450
Stacking ServiceOptional add-on
+$50–$100

Questions to Ask Any Tree Service

These are the six questions Aaron recommends asking any tree service you're comparing — not just Roubic. If a service can't answer them straightforwardly, that's a signal.

  1. Do you carry general liability + workers-comp insurance? Ask for a certificate.
  2. Do you use owned equipment or rentals? Rental gaps affect scheduling and cost reliability.
  3. Who is on the crew, and how long have they been with you? Tenured crews are safer and faster.
  4. Will you file the village permit? Pepper Pike, Moreland Hills, Gates Mills — you should not have to do this yourself.
  5. What does clean-up include? Full chip haul-off should be standard, not extra.
  6. Do you provide written estimates? If the answer is "we'll call you with a number," walk away.

Bottom Line — Aaron's Advice

Tree service pricing is not opaque — the range is well-established, and any legitimate service can quote confidently after a property walk. If someone can't give a number in person, they're not the right service.

If the estimate feels too low, it's usually because something's excluded — permit filing, chip haul, insurance documentation. Ask what's in the price, not what the price is. {{global.owner_name}} · Owner

Roubic estimates always show scope on paper before you book. If you want a free walk-through on your specific property, Aaron responds within one business day — no trip charge, no obligation.

Common Cost Guide Questions

Cost Guide FAQ

Are these prices the same across all 13 cities Roubic serves?
Yes — the base pricing is identical across all cities. Where estimates differ is response scheduling (Tier 1 priority vs Tier 3 2-3 day) and occasional village-permit filing costs (Pepper Pike, Moreland Hills, Gates Mills), which are included in the estimate scope, not billed separately.
Do you ever charge above the ranges shown?
Rarely. Very-large crane jobs (80+ ft trees over structures) or emergency after-hours callouts with restricted access can push above the top of the range. Aaron confirms the number in writing before booking — no surprises.
Are the estimates free?
Yes. Every Roubic estimate is free, includes an in-person property walk, and comes with a written scope + confirmed price. No trip charge, no obligation to book.
Do you match competitor prices?
No — Roubic prices on scope, not competitor comparison. If a competitor's estimate is significantly lower, Aaron will explain what's likely excluded (permit filing, chip haul, insurance documentation, unsecured crews) so you can compare apples to apples.
How often is this guide updated?
Annually — usually in January or February when Aaron reviews the prior year's job records and adjusts baseline pricing. This guide reflects 2026 pricing and will be updated in early 2027.
